neighbours.label: preposition after a school-stage word, expecting a school next: 'senior year in', 'graduating from', 'while still in', 'a junior in'
fire: He took up chess during his sophomore year in high school.
She met him right after graduating from college.
She wrote her first novel while she was still in school.
As a freshman in Ohio, she won the state title.
They married soon after he graduated from law school.
My junior year in college was the hardest of all.
He began coding as a senior in Denver.
He sold his first app while still in high school.
quiet: He took up chess during his long stay in Colorado.
She met him right after returning from Canada.
She wrote her first novel while she was living in Spain.
As a lawyer in Ohio, she won the state title.
They married soon after he returned from a trip.
My last week in Paris was the hardest of all.
He began coding as a clerk in Denver.
He sold his first app while working in sales.

notes: Output promotes ' college', ' university', ' undergraduate'; the - pole fires on ' school' and ' college'. Probes: ' in' after 'senior year' 0.91, 'junior' 0.77, 'while still' 0.87 (also before 'prison', since it can only see the prefix), ' from' after 'graduating' 0.67; 'moving from' 0.13. The peak comes on the preposition, before the school word.
